source_edition: Multidimensional Subjective Financial Well-Being Scale — original Italian emerging adults
measured_scales: General subjective financial well-being; Money management; Having money; Peer comparison; Financial future
target_population: Italian emerging adults, 2019 development and validity cohorts; age-tailored instrument.
EN_respondent_validation: IT-IT respondent-language original development and psychometric evaluation, five-factor final 25-item form.
RU_respondent_validation: No RU adaptation validated by this source; UI RU language does not count.
ES_respondent_validation: No ES adaptation validated by this source.
other_languages: Italian and Portuguese versions studied separately in original publication.
evidence_review: IT original: original 44-item draft reduced to 25 across five factors. 2019 article independently assessed Italian and Portuguese forms.

source_edition: Multidimensional Subjective Financial Well-Being Scale — Portuguese comparative validation
measured_scales: General subjective financial well-being; Money management; Having money; Peer comparison; Financial future
target_population: Portuguese emerging adults in original Italian/Portuguese measurement-invariance research.
EN_respondent_validation: The English-language paper reports an Italian original but does not itself establish a separate EN respondent-language validation.
ES_respondent_validation: No ES validated respondent-language edition evidenced.
other_languages: PT-PT Portuguese respondent-language invariance against Italian tested in original 2019 study; this is separate from Brazilian Portuguese.
evidence_review: PT-PT: Portuguese and Italian measurement invariance assessed on emerging-adult cohorts, not blanket Lusophone equivalence.

source_edition: Multidimensional Subjective Financial Well-Being Scale — Persian Iranian validation
measured_scales: General subjective financial well-being; Money management; Having money; Peer comparison; Financial future
target_population: 356 adults aged 18–29, Sanandaj Iran; gender, age, living, occupational group analyses.
EN_respondent_validation: English is article publication language, NOT evidence that English questionnaire administered in this Persian cohort.
other_languages: FA-IR Persian translated/adapted respondent-language edition independently CFA validated in Iranian emerging adults (2026).
evidence_review: FA-IR: 2026 study supports 25-item five-factor model and within-study invariance by gender/age/living/work; not generalized Iranian population norms.

source_edition: Multidimensional Subjective Financial Well-Being Scale — 2024 nine-country replication study
measured_scales: General subjective financial well-being; Money management; Having money; Peer comparison; Financial future
target_population: 4,475 emerging adults across nine countries, convenience/specific sampling; 2024.
EN_respondent_validation: Journal article EN; individual questionnaire respondent languages and equivalence NOT individually established by language from this cross-country row.
RU_respondent_validation: No new independently validated RU form in this record.
ES_respondent_validation: No new independently validated ES form in this record.
other_languages: Nine-country pooled/country-model evidence: Austria; Canada; Finland; India; Italy; Portugal; Romania; Slovenia; Turkey; do not map countries automatically to respondent languages.
evidence_review: Cross-country comparisons supported in some settings with limitations; this is replication/cohort evidence, NOT a new 25-item language edition; do not count nine countries as nine validated translations.

source_edition: InCharge Financial Distress/Financial Well-Being Scale — Brazilian Portuguese preliminary adaptation
measured_scales: Perceived financial distress versus financial well-being (single overall subjective continuum)
target_population: Brazilian adults aged 18–60; n=49 pre-test, n=60 reliability subgroup.
EN_respondent_validation: Original IFDFW EN8 exists as separate archive record; no new EN edition claimed.
RU_respondent_validation: No RU validated edition shown by this study.
ES_respondent_validation: No Spanish adaptation validated by this PT-BR study.
other_languages: PT-BR linguistic/cross-cultural adaptation and preliminary reliability documented; NOT the same as European Portuguese.
evidence_review: PT-BR preliminary adaptation/retest CCC .73 and alpha .878; modest samples mean not full national norms; article open access does not establish digital commercial rights.

source_edition: InCharge Financial Distress/Financial Well-Being Scale — Peru 2024 validation
measured_scales: Financial distress and perceived financial well-being (one-dimensional 8-item structure)
target_population: 545 adults from Peruvian coast, Andes and rainforest; age mean 33.45; publication May 5 2024.
EN_respondent_validation: Original EN8 belongs to preexisting source edition; not newly EN-validated here.
RU_respondent_validation: No RU validated adaptation in this study.
ES_respondent_validation: ES-PE Spanish administered and psychometrically evaluated on Peru 2024 sample.
other_languages: Peruvian ES-PE national context only; not all Spanish-speaking countries.
evidence_review: ES-PE n545 CFA one factor with correlated errors, alpha .881, CR .91; regional limits and correlated residuals preclude generic cutoffs.

source_edition: InCharge Financial Distress/Financial Well-Being Scale — Peru southern highlands 2025 independent validation
question_count: 8 (original IFDFW form; independently confirm final local item list before use)
measured_scales: Financial distress / subjective financial well-being (single common factor)
target_population: 1059 workers aged 18–65, Cuzco, Arequipa, Puno, Peru; 2025 source.
EN_respondent_validation: English article abstract is NOT proof of English instrument respondent language.
RU_respondent_validation: No RU validation from this record.
ES_respondent_validation: ES-PE locally translated and adapted financial well-being questionnaire independently CFA tested among Peruvian working adults.
other_languages: ES-PE target cohort is highland workers; distinguish 2024 Peruvian mixed-regions cohort, no new Spanish universal norms.
evidence_review: Separate ES-PE validation cohort; CFA CFI .992, RMSEA .063, SRMR .027, omega .82, gender/work invariance; exact administered item-by-item wording requires source appendix check.

source_edition: Money Attitude Scale — Yamauchi and Templer original 29-item final form
measured_scales: Power–prestige; Retention–time; Distrust; Anxiety (quality was exploratory fifth factor, not retained in final 29)
target_population: Original US adult/community sample, initial item pool 62; psychometric samples described by 1982 journal.
EN_respondent_validation: EN original developed in original 1982 psychometric paper; respondent language associated with original USA cohort.
RU_respondent_validation: No RU adaptation for this original edition independently verified.
ES_respondent_validation: No ES validation for this exact original edition verified.
other_languages: Other respondent-language validity requires specific source/edition research.
evidence_review: Final 29-item instrument retained four factors out of exploratory five; do not treat initial exploratory Quality factor as validated final subscale.

source_edition: A New Money Attitudes Questionnaire — Lay and Furnham
measured_scales: Achievement and success; Power and status; Mindful and responsible; Saving concerns; Financial literacy worries
EN_respondent_validation: EN-language original 30-item validation (published 2019), online sample n268.
other_languages: Do not infer other translations from Anglophone article.
evidence_review: Study supports a proposed five-factor model (EFA/CFA); distinct from 29-item New Money Behavior Quiz and 1982 Money Attitude Scale.

source_edition: Money Madness Facet Questionnaire — Furnham and Horne preliminary 52-item
measured_scales: Security; Power; Love; Freedom (three conceptual facets per higher-order factor, partial empirical support)
target_population: 256 online adults of varied backgrounds, Furnham & Horne 2021.
EN_respondent_validation: English-language original preliminary online respondents; 52 items.
other_languages: Other locale editions have not been substantiated by this source.
evidence_review: Four broad factors internally consistent but some facet reliability unsatisfactory and factor structure only partially replicated; exploratory metadata, not a fully validated instrument.

source_edition: A New Money Behavior Quiz — Furnham and Grover original
measured_scales: Six a priori money-behaviour types devised by financial practitioners; exploratory and modest reliability
EN_respondent_validation: English original 29-item participant questionnaire, journal paper 2020 (online 2019).
RU_respondent_validation: Russian Nestik–Gagarina 2022 12-item, four-factor adaptation is a DISTINCT shortened/localized model; cannot transfer English norms or 6-type score.
evidence_review: Original 29-item six-type model had modest internal reliability; do not treat six expert-proposed types as independently strong clinical diagnostic subscales.

source_edition: New Money Behavior Quiz — Russian Nestik/Gagarina 12-item four-factor revision
question_count: 12 (four 3-item factors in published final version; verify source PDF appendix before activating)
measured_scales: Financial obsession; Money as social respect/status; Money as influence/power; Financial anxiety
target_population: 2994 Russian adults in Dec 2020 online cohort, mean age 40.5; independent 500-person construct validity check.
EN_respondent_validation: English 29-item Furnham–Grover original is a different item-count/scoring version; no English validity claim for Russian 12-item form.
RU_respondent_validation: RU-RU psychometrically validated Russian respondent-language version in Russian adults, 2022 published.
other_languages: Non-RU respondent-language translations not independently evaluated in this 2022 validation.
evidence_review: RU: 2022 four-factor CFA preferred to six-factor model; independent construct-validity n500; journal article CC BY-NC 4.0 explicitly noncommercial, so NO permission to use translated items/scoring on for-profit Holistic House.

source_edition: Express Questionnaire on Debt Behaviour — Russian validated brief form
measured_scales: Debt rationality vs irrationality; Debt avoidance vs acceptance; Condemnation vs tolerance of debtors
target_population: 1058 Russian respondents aged 17–82, mean age 24.9; Gagarina and Padun, 2021.
EN_respondent_validation: Russian-developed test; no independent original EN respondent-language edition established.
RU_respondent_validation: RU-RU native authored/developed shortened 14-item version CFA validated in Russian respondent sample.
ES_respondent_validation: No independent Spanish respondent-language validation established.
other_languages: Other localized language forms require separate validation.
evidence_review: RU: 14 items, three factors confirmed by CFA and reliability/validity deemed acceptable in source abstract. Authors/publisher digital commercial license NOT established.
